page: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Featuring 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at clock speeds up to 3.7 GHz, this x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 extensions, bfloat16, VNNI, and hardware cryptography instructions such as AES and SHA-NI. The server is configured with 768 GB of system memory, delivering a ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, and bundles 23,040 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage. It does not include discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results place the system in the top tier for multi-threaded performance. Multi-core execution ranks in the top decile on stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU suites. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth exceeds 229 GB/sec for reads and 140 GB/sec for writes. The platform also exhibits high throughput under sustained concurrent operations, recording 122.77 million SET operations per second in Redis benchmarks. Workloads involving Clang compilation, ray tracing, and multi-threaded decompression similarly show top-tier execution, supported by strong single-core scores exceeding 2000 in Geekbench.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server combines substantial multi-core density, high memory allocations, and massive integrated NVMe storage into a single node. This resource combination reduces the need to maintain separate storage fabrics or multi-node clusters for data-heavy operations. The primary technical tradeoff involves managing data resilience on ephemeral local NVMe volumes, along with the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is designed for workloads requiring low-latency storage access, high compute concurrency, and large memory footprints. Primary use cases include distributed databases, enterprise NoSQL datastores, real-time in-memory caching layers, data warehousing, and large parallel build environments.
description: Microsoft Azure L96as_v4 is a storage-optimized instance tailored for data-intensive and high-throughput workloads. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, the virtual machine provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with clock speeds up to 3.7 GHz. It integrates 768 GB of system memory alongside 23,040 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage, omitting discrete GPUs to dedicate resources entirely to compute and I/O capacity. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-core computing capability in PassMark and Geekbench, complemented by memory read bandwidth exceeding 229 GB/sec and in-memory Redis processing reaching 122.77 million SET operations per second. The allocation of 8 GB RAM per vCPU combined with extensive local NVMe capacity delivers high resource consolidation for I/O-intensive demands. This hardware profile suits large transactional databases, NoSQL distributed data stores, in-memory caching systems, and demanding software compilation workloads.
